title: A weakly universal element from a perfect generating family
statement: Let C be a pretriangulated category with Hom universe v and all v-small coproducts. Let S_j be a family indexed in universe v, shift closed up to isomorphism, which detects zero objects and is perfect: componentwise surjectivity on Hom from all S_j is preserved by v-small coproducts. Let H:C^op to Ab_v be cohomological and send v-small coproducts to products. There exist X in C and x in H(X) such that every y in H(Y), for every Y in C, equals H(f)(x) for some f:Y to X.

source.place: Krause, Derived categories, resolutions, and Brown representability, Section 4.5, cellular Brown construction and extension from generators.

proof.text: Convert preservation of discrete limits by H to the elementwise coproduct/product property using the forgetful functor to types and Types.isLimit_iff. Convert H.IsHomological to exactness on the first two maps of a distinguished triangle using H.map_distinguished_op_exact and ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff.

Given (W,w), start with W plus the coproduct indexed by all pairs (j,z in H(S_j)), with its universal element. From (X_n,x_n), form the evaluation coproduct of all maps S_j to X_n killed by x_n, and take its cone. Product preservation makes the pullback of x_n zero; exactness lifts it to x_(n+1). Every such kernel map dies after this transition. Iterate this proved construction using Nat.rec.

Take the telescope of the tower. The source Telescope.exists_lift produces a compatible element; perfectFamily_telescope_bijective proves that its evaluation is bijective on every S_j. The map from the seed W respects elements.

If a map between pairs universally representing H on the S_j respects their elements, its maps on Hom(S_j,-) are bijective. Complete it to a distinguished triangle. Shift closure and the Hom exact sequence show every map from S_j to its cone vanishes; zero detection makes the cone zero and hence the map an isomorphism.

Approximate the zero seed to get (X,x). For arbitrary (Y,y), approximate X plus Y with element (x,y). The resulting map X to the approximation is an isomorphism by the preceding step. Compose the map from Y with its inverse. Functoriality shows that this pulls x back to y.

proof_origin.place: Explicit cellular cone/telescope construction and the zero-cone argument.

lean.statement:
theorem perfectFamily_exists_weakUniversal
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C]
    [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{v} C]
    {J : Type v} (S : J → C)
    (hshift : ∀ (j : J) (n : ℤ), ∃ k, Nonempty (S k ≅ (S j)⟦n⟧))
    (hzero : ∀ X : C, (∀ j (f : S j ⟶ X), f = 0) → IsZero X)
    (hperfect : ∀ (I : Type v) (X Y : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i),
      (∀ i j, Function.Surjective (fun g : S j ⟶ X i ↦ g ≫ f i)) →
      ∀ j, Function.Surjective (fun g : S j ⟶ ∐ X ↦ g ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f))
    (H : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.IsHomological]
    (hH : ∀ I : Type v, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) H) :
    ∃ (X : C) (x : H.obj (op X)),
      ∀ (Y : C) (y : H.obj (op Y)), ∃ f : Y ⟶ X, H.map f.op x = y
